settingName: an early Imperial Roman marching camp on a dry temperate frontier plain
settingDescription: A slightly raised dry-grass site beside one dusty approach road, surrounded by low hills. The temporary camp uses a shallow outer ditch, a low inward earthen rampart reinforced with simple wooden stakes, restrained gate openings, straight internal lanes and muted brown leather tents. No stone fortifications or permanent barracks.
recurringPlaces: the same rectangular temporary camp footprint on the low rise
the same near gate facing the dusty approach road
the same dry-grass terrain and low hills surrounding the camp
recurringCharacters: one recurring legionary with short dark hair, short beard, muted rust-red tunic, dark belt, brown sandals and simple early Imperial Roman military equipment
recurringProps: simple wooden stakes and entrenching tools
rectangular Roman shields and packed marching gear
timeWeatherLogic: The sequence progresses continuously from late afternoon to dusk, then night, then pale dawn; the weather remains dry and calm throughout.
continuityRules: For recurring locations, preserve silhouette, layout, openings, materials and defining props.
For before/after or changing-state scenes, reuse the same or nearly the same viewpoint when that makes the change clearer.
For recurring people, preserve hair, beard, headwear, clothing colors and identifying props.
The camp never becomes a permanent stone fortress; all defenses remain temporary earth, timber and leather construction.
Bild 03, Bild 07 and Bild 10 must clearly read as the same terrain from closely related elevated viewpoints.
